pack.title: Credit stealers
pack.description: Reclaim credit without derailing the meeting.

scenarios.setting: A colleague presents your analysis in a team meeting without credit.
scenarios.jab: I put together this analysis over the weekend.
scenarios.goal: Reclaim credit without derailing the meeting.

replies.line: I led the analysis. Happy to explain how we reached these numbers.
replies.why: Naming your contribution restores authorship while keeping the discussion on the work.
replies.delivery: Stress “led the analysis,” keep your voice even, then describe the work.

replies.line: That analysis is mine. Here's the method.
replies.why: It corrects the attribution and immediately supplies useful context.
replies.delivery: Say “That analysis is mine” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. Then describe the work.

replies.line: Thanks for walking everyone through my analysis; I can cover the next steps.
replies.why: Acknowledging their presentation while naming your work separates presenting from creating.
replies.delivery: Keep “Thanks for walking everyone through my analysis” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. Then describe the work.

replies.line: The spreadsheet and I spent a lot of quality time together.
replies.why: Light humor signals your involvement without accusing your colleague of bad intent.
replies.delivery: Keep “The spreadsheet and I spent a lot of” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. Then describe the work.

followUp.line: Yes, and I led the analysis; let's list everyone's contributions accurately.
followUp.why: It recognizes collaboration without withdrawing your specific claim.
followUp.delivery: Stress “led the analysis,” keep your voice even, then describe the work.
